newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline margin gains offset sales - analysts.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline margin gains offset sales - analysts.

text.p: Analysts on Tuesday expressed some disappointment over the growth in SmithKline Beecham Plc's pharmaceutical sales in the first quarter of the year, but said this was offset by gains in trading profit margins.

Earlier, SmithKline said pharmaceutical sales were up by 12 percent in the first three months of 1997, excluding the impact of currency changes and the Diversified Pharmaceutical Services benefit management business.

However, Williams de Broe analyst Peter Cartwright said the market had been looking for growth of 13 to 14 percent in this key figure. "It was not quite as good as we'd hoped, but the trading profit clearly is," said Cartwright.
SocGen analyst Paul Diggle said the SmithKline sales advance was disappointing in comparison with its U.S. peer group.
"We have had some terrific numbers out of the U.S," Diggle said, with gains ranging from 14 to 20 percent.

Shares in the company were up 17 pence at 923 in midafternoon trade, with analysts locked into a telephone conference with senior managers. However they were trading off a high of 935 pence hit before the results were announced.
Diggle said that only Sweden's Astra AB and Switzerland's Roche Holding AG had so far posted lower first-quarter sales growth figures.
"So that is not quite as good as we'd hoped," Diggle added.
He said follow-through in the Consumer Healthcare business from a very strong fourth-quarter had also not been as positive as some had hoped.
But with sales up an underlying 18 percent and trading profits up 20 percent, "this was nevertheless a pretty good performance," Diggle said.
Overall, Diggle said, the results were, "fine but not enough to excite very much".

"It will probably be the best quarter in terms of underlying growth but it will also be the worst for currency, so I think we will keep with our view for the year," said Diggle, who is predicting an 11 percent rise in pre-tax profits to 1.73 billion stg.
Cartwright added that the first quarter was never the company's best quarter and said it may have been deliberately cautious.
"There was a dull first quarter last year and too high a figure (this time) could have sent the wrong signal for the rest of the year," he said.
